notes.7: In this exercise candidates are required to transfer information from the text provided, and total accuracy is required when filling in the person’s contact details. On the whole, candidates did not have difficulties in finding the correct information they needed in order to complete the form. Our repeated request has been to ensure while writing the address candidates always follow the correct order. For instance, first mention the house number then the apartment name and then the city name. This year most candidates correctly wrote the address; very few candidates still made these mistakes. Exercise 3 Questions 8–10 The topic of this year’s text was about a declining folk form from Rajasthan called ‘Swang’. Most candidates did very well in this exercise.

notes.11: For this summary-writing exercise, there were up to six marks available for Content and up to four marks available for Language. This year, most candidates appeared to be well prepared for the requirements of this exercise and generally performed well. Many candidates wrote their summaries in their own words and were therefore able to access the full range of marks available for Language. Most candidates managed to select 5 or 6 correct points from the text and managed to secure 2 or 3 marks for Language. Few candidates scored full marks for Language. The majority of candidates confined their answer to within the word limit. However, a small minority of candidates still exceeded the word limit. Very few candidates wrote their points without following the format of summary writing. Section 2 Exercise 5 Questions 11–18 This year most candidates performed very well in this exercise. Questions 11–14 involved candidates studying a statement and selecting whether that statement was true or false. A small number of candidates unnecessarily included the justification for correct statements. According to the rubric, if the given statement is correct, there is no need to provide the justification. For Questions 15 to 17 , most candidates gave correct answers. Some candidates wrote the answer for Question 16 in place of Question 15 . Question 15 was: “what has Abdul done in order to prove the influence Hindu religion has had on him?”. The correct answer was that he sang a religious song or some couplets. However, a few candidates wrote that he put up a picture of the Taj Mahal on his wall instead. This could not be credited as correct answer for Question 15 . Exercise 6 This year’s essay topic was on whether significance of the joint family is declining. Candidates had to suggest their personal views on the topic and justify why they were in support of or against the idea of the joint family. Most candidates attempted the exercise successfully. The candidates who scored good marks in this exercise included economic reasons like lack of space, high prices and the nature of work which forces some joint families to split. Several candidates underlined the importance of not spending enough time with the family and they cited different reasons for it. Many candidates blamed technology such as television, computers and mobile phones for making individuals spend less time with their families. However, not all candidates gave combinations of reasons and elaborated appropriately. More time should be devoted to teaching the basic mechanics of writing in Hindi. Sometimes frequent spelling errors hindered the meaning and made it difficult to understand what candidates were trying to say. The spelling mistakes were threefold in nature. Firstly, the vowel sounds ‘Ee’ were used incorrectly. Secondly, the aspirated letters were written with non aspirated letters in Hindi. Thirdly, the conjunct in Hindi especially with the letter ‘Ra’ was not used correctly. Teachers should encourage their candidates to think in Hindi to make their writing more fluent. It seemed that some candidates were planning the content and what to write in English, and then they translated their thoughts into Hindi. This caused problems with the syntax of the writing. For example, some candidates 0549 Hindi as a Second Language June 2014 used the word in Hindi for ‘clever’ in a positive context whereas the same word has a negative connotation in Hindi which made its use inappropriate. 0549 Hindi as a Second Language June 2014 HINDI AS A SECOND LANGUAGE
